title: Expected Mac Reports System Integrity Protection Disabled
exclusions: Compares expected Macs with normalized Apple MDM security/device-information query results for System Integrity Protection (SIP). It reports no result in 48 hours, a result older than 24 hours, an unknown value, or explicit `sip_enabled=false`. It deliberately removes Gatekeeper from this UC because Apple documents SIP as a queryable yes/no state while Gatekeeper is a separately managed security-payload policy. SIP enabled does not attest Secure Boot policy, Gatekeeper policy/effective assessment, kernel-extension approval, malware absence, or regulatory compliance.
evidence: Retain the `expected_macos_sip_disabled` saved search, daily schedule, results and alerts; expected-device and exception lookup revisions; redacted MDM query/response IDs, SIP boolean, status and collection times; API/command health; fixtures; dashboard/case history; recovery response; and approved exception or lifecycle evidence. This documentation-only review queried no Mac or MDM and produced no production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z add expected IDs `sip-off`, `sip-stale`, and `sip-missing`. Index `sip-off` at 11:00 with `sip_enabled=false`; index `sip-stale` true at 2026-07-28T11:59:59Z; index nothing for missing. Expect exactly three rows: `sip_disabled`, `status_stale` age 86401, and `not_observed_in_48h`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Require zero rows for true SIP status exactly 86400 seconds old or newer; inactive/future/expired/non-macOS inventory; an observed but unexpected ID; or a finding with an exact future exception containing reason, ticket, and owner. Expiry equal to dispatch does not suppress. A Gatekeeper-anywhere policy or reduced Secure Boot state remains separate.

dataSources: Apple MDM SecurityInfo or device-information query exported through the selected device-management service's documented API/webhook. Required normalized fields are `_time`, exact `device_id`, `platform`, boolean `sip_enabled`, `response_status`, `command_id`, `collector_time`, `tenant`, and `collector_version`; retain vendor request/pagination health. `index=endpoint_posture`, `sourcetype=local:apple:security_status`, aliases, and lookup names are local conventions. A local `csrutil status` parser is not mixed into this remote source without a separate qualified contract.
app: Apple device management protocol and the selected MDM vendor supply SIP query state. A deployment-owned collector and Splunk search app provide normalization, inventory, exceptions, fixtures, search, dashboard, and runbook. Gatekeeper payload compliance belongs in a separate policy control; no Splunkbase add-on is asserted.
spl:
| inputlookup expected_macos_sip.csv
| eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), monitor_from_epoch=tonumber(monitor_from_epoch), monitor_until_epoch=tonumber(monitor_until_epoch), expected_row=1
| where lower(trim(monitor_enabled))="true" AND platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0 AND monitor_from_epoch<=now() AND monitor_until_epoch>now()
| fields device_id expected_row device_name serial_number owner criticality runbook
| append [ search index=endpoint_posture sourcetype=local:apple:security_status earliest=-48h latest=now
    | eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), sip_enabled=case(sip_enabled=true() OR lower(trim(sip_enabled))="true",1,sip_enabled=false() OR lower(trim(sip_enabled))="false",0,true(),null()), observed_row=1
    | where platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0
    | stats latest(_time) AS status_time latest(sip_enabled) AS sip_enabled latest(response_status) AS response_status latest(command_id) AS command_id latest(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id ]
| stats max(expected_row) AS expected_row max(observed_row) AS observed_row values(device_name) AS device_name values(serial_number) AS serial_number values(owner) AS owner values(criticality) AS criticality values(runbook) AS runbook max(status_time) AS status_time max(sip_enabled) AS sip_enabled values(response_status) AS response_status values(command_id) AS command_id max(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id
| where expected_row=1
| eval status_age_seconds=if(isnull(status_time),null(),now()-status_time), finding=case(isnull(observed_row),"not_observed_in_48h",isnull(sip_enabled),"unknown_sip_value",sip_enabled=0,"sip_disabled",status_age_seconds>86400,"status_stale",true(),"healthy")
| where finding!="healthy"
| lookup macos_sip_exceptions.csv device_id OUTPUT exception_until_epoch exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval stale_threshold_seconds=86400, observation_window_hours=48, use_case_id="UC-1.3.3"
| table device_id device_name serial_number finding sip_enabled status_time status_age_seconds response_status command_id collector_time owner criticality runbook stale_threshold_seconds observation_window_hours use_case_id
| sort 0 finding -status_age_seconds device_id
description: Runs daily and emits one row per active expected Mac when its latest MDM-reported SIP state is absent for 48 hours, unknown, false, or strictly older than 24 hours. The grain is exact lowercased device-management ID and each row retains response, command, age, inventory, and owner context.
value: Disabled SIP weakens macOS protections against modification of protected system components, while absent or stale posture data creates a separate visibility gap. Exact inventory-first findings let endpoint and security teams distinguish deliberate recovery/development work, identity drift, and collection failure without claiming Gatekeeper or Secure Boot coverage.
implementation: Export Apple's queryable SIP boolean through the MDM's supported API, preserve query and collection health, normalize booleans without guessing, and reconcile exact expected device IDs. Run daily with 48-hour observation and strict 24-hour freshness, alert by device/finding, and use finite exact exceptions. Validate against a controlled Mac and MDM console; investigate recoveryOS/security-policy changes through approved endpoint procedures.
visualization: Put MDM query freshness, failures, expected coverage, unknown values, and duplicate IDs first. Then show SIP disabled/stale/absent by owner, model, site, and status age with trend history. Drill down to redacted MDM response, startup-security evidence, approved recovery/developer change, exception, incident, and restored status. Keep Gatekeeper and Secure Boot panels separate.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; no CIM mapping is asserted for Apple SIP state or expected-device absence.

knownFalsePositives:
A finding is valid under the evidence contract but can have an approved cause.

1. **Authorized recoveryOS or developer work** — SIP may be disabled for tightly controlled diagnostics. Verify physical/recovery authorization, owner, device, purpose, start/end, rollback, and post-change query; never accept an indefinite exception.

2. **OS repair, migration, or re-enrollment** — Device ID/status can change. Reconcile serial, old/new MDM IDs, enrollment and asset lifecycle before updating inventory.

3. **MDM command or API failure** — Timeout, permission loss, pagination, or collector outage creates stale/absent results. Check response status, command ID, canary, totals, and collection time before endpoint action.

4. **Boolean normalization defect** — Null, localized UI text, or vendor enum mapped incorrectly can become unknown/false. Compare raw redacted response, vendor schema, parser version, and fixtures.

**Suppression mechanism:** the SPL uses `lookup macos_sip_exceptions.csv` on exact `device_id` and requires future expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. Expired, wildcard, fleet-wide, MDM-outage, Gatekeeper, or Secure-Boot exceptions do not suppress.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Apple SIP security/device-information queries, startup security, system-extension behavior and separate Gatekeeper payload guidance plus Splunk lookup/scheduled-alert documentation; MDM/macOS/Splunk versions, API, fields, inventory, SPL, fixtures, freshness, exceptions, source health, alert delivery, startup-security response, and production behavior were specified but not executed or Apple/MDM/Splunk/endpoint/security/SME signed
detailedImplementation:
## Scope and prerequisites

Assign MDM, macOS/startup-security, asset, security, Splunk, service-desk, and change owners. Qualify MDM API, macOS, collector, and Splunk versions; this review ran none. Give the collector only device/security-query read access and protect tenant/request metadata. Apple documents SIP as a yes/no security query. Gatekeeper is configured through separate security payloads and is intentionally excluded instead of combining unlike fields.

Export each query result with exact tenant/device/command identity, SIP boolean, response status, device status time, API collection time, pagination and collector version. Normalize true/false/null through vendor-schema fixtures; do not parse a UI label. Keep a local `csrutil` collector separate if adopted because boot context, command output, and endpoint trust differ. Monitor newest successful query, canary, errors, object totals, pagination, null rate, duplicate IDs, and indexing delay.

Create `expected_macos_sip.csv` with unique device ID, platform, enabled flag, lifecycle epochs, serial, owner, criticality, and runbook. Reconcile against MDM and asset records. Govern `macos_sip_exceptions.csv` by exact ID, finite UTC expiry, purpose, ticket, and owner.

## Search and validation

Save `expected_macos_sip_disabled`, run daily, and trigger per device/finding. The lookup creates absence; the event branch keeps newest 48-hour state; exactly 86400 seconds is accepted and 86401 is stale. Route a broad stale/absent burst to MDM/data owners before endpoint teams.

Run fixed controls plus true/false/null/string values, 86399/86400/86401 ages, no event, newer duplicate, wrong platform, lifecycle and exception equality, re-enrollment, API failure, late indexing, and multiple OS/security-policy configurations. On a lab Mac, compare MDM state before and after an approved SIP change performed through Apple's required startup-security process; do not disable production SIP merely to test. Keep draft until owners accept source semantics, versions, tests, freshness, alerting, and response.

## Response and troubleshooting

Verify collector/query health and a canary first; then exact identity/lifecycle; latest MDM response; approved recovery/developer work; startup security, Secure Boot, OS instance, system-extension requirements, and recent repair/reinstall. SIP can differ from Gatekeeper and, on Apple silicon, security policy is associated with an installed OS, so preserve boot-volume context in the runbook.

Do not automate SIP changes, recoveryOS entry, Secure Boot reduction, kernel-extension approval, Gatekeeper changes, restart, wipe, or re-enrollment from Splunk. Those require physical/endpoint authority and rollback. Close after a new authoritative true SIP result and separate validation of any affected extension/application. If all devices stale, repair MDM/query collection; if one device false, investigate device/change; if true but Gatekeeper weak, use the separate policy control; if status is unknown, fix extraction rather than treating unknown as disabled or healthy.
grandmaExplanation: We ask the Mac management service whether each expected Mac still has System Integrity Protection on. Missing, old, or off answers are investigated; Gatekeeper and startup security are checked separately.
